text:
maria: hitting a weird thing with redwoodctl on my local machine — using a symlinked ~/.redwoodctl (dotfiles) and the token keeps expiring during `redwood local serve`. login works but after a minute requests get 401
kevin: hm, do you mean the credentials file is a symlink to the dotfiles repo?
maria: yep. .redwoodctl -> ~/dotfiles/redwood/credentials. redwoodctl login writes the token but the server process seems to read an older copy or not follow the link
sam: can you share the exact error? 401 body or "token expired"?
maria: curl to localhost:8080 returns 401 with: "invalid_auth: token not found" from the local auth middleware. CLI shows successful login and the credentials file contains the new token
lucas: I've seen this with other CLIs — some runtimes open the file once and then keep the fd, so if you replace the target of a symlink the process doesn't see the new file. If login writes by nuking the file and recreating it you can end up with an inode mismatch
kevin: try `redwoodctl login --profile devbox --no-replace` (forces in-place update) or `redwoodctl login && pkill -HUP redwood-local` — forcing the local server to reload credentials. also check permissions: if the dotfiles repo is 770 the server user might not follow it
maria: trying the HUP trick now... ok sending a new request — still 401
sam: can you run `strace -e openat -p $(pgrep redwood-local)` while doing a login to watch which path it's opening? if it opens the original path vs the symlink target it's the inode case
maria: starting strace... looks like the server opened ~/.redwoodctl/credentials at startup and keeps the fd. It never re-opens on reqs
lucas: yeah that's it. Two practical workarounds: 1) make the credentials file writable in-place (so login updates the same inode), or 2) set REDWOODCTL_TOKEN_PATH to a non-symlink absolute path and point the server at that file while you keep the symlink in dotfiles for your shell tools
kevin: we're going to add an explicit reload on SIGHUP in the local server so it re-reads credentials (tracking: DEVEX-456). short term: `ln -f ~/dotfiles/redwood/credentials ~/.redwoodctl/credentials && chmod 600 ~/.redwoodctl/credentials` (ensures same inode)
maria: that worked — in-place link + chmod fixed it. thanks all. putting workaround in the README for local dev
infra-bot: note added to DEVEX-456: "local server should watch credential file or support runtime reload" :eyes:
maria: filed a tiny PR to README with the env var hint and the ln workaround, will add a test to reproduce the inode/symlink case later :thumbsup:
